newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebels demand talks with Fujimori.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebels demand talks with Fujimori.

text.p: Peruvian rebels holding 200 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima demanded on Wednesday that President Alberto Fujimori personally join in negotiations.

"The only thing I want to say is that the president must come and speak to us personally. Nothing will happen to him, we only want dialogue," a Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrilla spokesman inside the residence told a local radio station.

Fujimori has so far not commented publicly on the situation. However, in a conversation with Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, he said Interior Minister Juan Briones Davila was handling negotiations.
Countries with ambassadors inside the building have urged Fujimori to do everything in his power to protect the hostages and not use force to flush out the rebels.

The rebel spokesman also demanded the presence of Peru's ombudsman, Jorge Santistevan, and Roman Catholic priest Hubert Lanssiers, who sits on a government-appointed panel that recommends pardons for Peruvians wrongly jailed on terrorism charges.
